# Housekeeping: effect-contract

## Authorized scope and smallest closable slice

Review the complete `crates/effect-contract` Cargo package and its tests. Deliver practical, behavior-preserving cleanup in this package, or an evidenced no-change verdict when existing choices earn their cost. Cover all five user requests: repeated code/LoC; load-bearing test purposes; avoidable copies; applicable micro SIMD; and data structures that cap efficiency. The user requests two GPT-6.1 Sol xhigh agents concurrently; this overrides the default Terra implementation model for this workflow. Root Sol owns briefing, adversarial review, exact-path checkpoints, integration and remote synchronization.

## Frozen boundaries

Existing public APIs, feature behavior, canonical/wire identities, arithmetic order and per-lane rendered bits, latency/tail, link modes, smoothing and NaN/denormal rules remain contractual. Zero render allocations/frees, locks, I/O or syscalls; no runtime native ISA dispatch. Retain scalar tails, 4-lane Wasm/NEON and x86 AVX2/FMA. Preserve all feature and target configurations. Do not expand another open issue or change DSP algorithms. Read current related issue bodies before touching their subject; discoveries that require architecture or product decisions become bounded follow-ups and final owner questions.

## Implementation and test-value decisions

Prefer deleting or consolidating repetition to adding abstractions that increase total complexity. Assess every existing test or a clearly named homogeneous family by its plausible unique defect; remove trivial, redundant or obsolete cases only after identifying the surviving behavioral gate. Keep independent numeric/oracle, fault, allocation, queue, boundary and target tests. Add/rewrite tests only for a concrete uncovered defect, and state which plausible defect no existing test catches. No prose/source-grep tests, new bit-digest pins or exact resource-byte pins. Copies needed for ownership, snapshots or atomic admission stay unless the same semantics are proved with less work. Data structure changes must preserve deterministic order and bounded realtime work. Inspect applicable hot loops and generated code before claiming additional SIMD; recursive/stateful dependencies alone do not justify changing arithmetic.

## Objective gates and evidence

- Read all production and test files in this package; record concise findings for each of the five requests, concrete changed/deferred locations, and load-bearing test families with retained coverage for deletions.
- Run focused locked package tests and affected feature configurations; use existing downstream/RT/differential gates proportional to the changed contract. Check formatting and package clippy with warnings denied. Relevant Wasm and AArch64 compile checks are required for changed product code; record limitations candidly.
- Changes to DSP arithmetic or hot state need existing independent numeric and scalar/SIMD gates plus one-time base/head evidence when needed; no permanent comparison against the old implementation. Existing research remains the algorithm authority; no new algorithm or listening claim is authorized.
- Benchmarks are optional and descriptive. Any timed measurement freezes its workload/validator, passes zero-workload preflight, and runs exactly one invocation with one warmup/two measured rounds. No timing optimization loop, performance percentage or unsupported sound-quality claim.
- Root conducts one adversarial verdict per coherent attempt, at most five total attempts. Every new/rewritten test gets its unique-defect sentence in that verdict. No-change audits require the same five-axis review, not manufactured edits.
- Stop after a coherent compiling, focused-green tranche; root commits exact owned paths before further edits. Keep edits within `crates/effect-contract` and this numbered spec. Independent crates use separate worktrees. Root pushes promptly and updates this GitHub issue with evidence; close only after PASS and evidence upstream, verifying remote state. Merge through the required qualification check and remove clean completed worktrees.

## Sol brief approval and decision record

Approved 2026-10-01 by root Sol within the user's crate-by-crate housekeeping request. Attempt 1 is authorized with the frozen scope/gates above. Owner questions are collected for the final report; routine reversible cleanup proceeds autonomously. Scope is this package's housekeeping, not completion of pre-existing feature/bug issues.

Reviewed all six source files, all six integration test files, the manifest and `tests/MUTATIONS.md`. **Five-axis findings and changes**

- Repetition/LoC: descriptor/port ID checking now uses the existing const `EffectId::new` validator, preserving length/character checks and error precedence. Identical Linear/Exponential default-lattice arms share one match. Existing bank dispatch, payload-size and semantic validation helpers already centralize their laws; wider abstractions would increase scope/complexity. Rust change: **+22/−129, net −107 lines**, including tests; no manifest/dependency or public API changes.
- Test value: removed five redundant/type-only tests and two exact internal Rust size assertions. Preserved the 64-byte control-record ceiling and the semantic twelve-word target count. No test was added; surviving endpoint tests received the removed assertions, as mapped below.
- Copies: continuous intrinsic points iterate minimum, default, optional maximum directly, preserving insertion/error order while removing the temporary `Vec`. Positive-exponent decimal padding extends its owned string directly instead of allocating a second zero string. Factory `Arc` clones remain necessary for plan ownership; state/target handoffs, retained buffers and live-control storage are unchanged. Bypass materialization belongs to #892; enum projection into the public slice-based lattice API remains bounded control-plane work.
- Micro SIMD: tile transpose helpers already use `Simd4`/AVX2 `Simd8`. An uncommitted optimized wrapper inspection (`/tmp/issue1120-transpose-probe.s`, rustc 1.97.1, +avx2,+fma) shows vector loads, unpack/shuffle/permutation instructions and stores for both widths, with no calls or stack spills; the by-value array API needed no change. Stateful smoothers, window folding and ordered staging retain their arithmetic/dependency order. No SIMD or DSP arithmetic was changed.
- Data structures: the private registry retains a `BTreeMap`, keyed by the IDs' already-static strings. Borrowed string lookups now use ordered `get` rather than scanning all entries. `EffectId`'s derived ordering is the same lexical string order; duplicate rejection and descriptor order remain unchanged. Live queues, target FIFOs, observation slots and sorted last-wins staging remain preallocated/bounded. No new resource cap or timing claim.

**Deletion → surviving behavioral gate**

- `cents_lattice_retains_round_endpoint_and_declared_default` → `declared_bounds_and_default_are_always_members`, retaining the same 10/20000 bounds, 80 default and intrinsic flags; the default's flag moved into the survivor. It rejects a generated default misclassified as a regular grid point.
- `ratio_lattice_retains_butterworth_default` → `geometric_ratio_row_keeps_its_round_maximum_and_meaningful_default`, retaining Q's exact intrinsic default/conversion and its 18 maximum assertion. It rejects either quantized Butterworth Q or an omitted round maximum.
- `prepared_target_has_frozen_copy_shape` → `prepared_control_record_stays_within_the_frozen_sixty_four_byte_bound` retains the record ceiling and twelve-word count. Copy derives and real queue/target handoffs already require the copyable types; exact `size_of::<PreparedEffectTarget>() == 56` is neither a wire identity nor a resource ceiling.
- `target_preparation_trait_is_object_safe` → production `NativeEffectFactory::target_preparation` returns the actual trait object, so every product build already rejects loss of object safety. Runtime target FIFO/error/reset tests remain.
- `retained_bytes_are_a_formula_over_the_declared_menu` → observation arm/fold/disarm tests and rack's `an_unobserved_bank_slot_reports_no_observation_state_at_all` retain declared tap counts, positive retained storage and unchanged storage after disarm. The deleted getter comparison could not observe an allocation/free, so it was not an allocation gate; existing measured RT conformance remains.

### Root adversarial review — attempt 1

Root adversarial verdict: PASS. Reviewed all six changed files. The private validator delegates to identical byte-domain checks in the same error order; lexical string keys preserve EffectId's derived order and duplicate identity while eliminating linear lookup scans. Intrinsic-point iteration preserves minimum/default/maximum insertion order, and direct ASCII padding preserves exponent bounds and resulting decimals. Neither change touches render arithmetic or ownership. The removed observation getter test could not detect allocation, and actual trait-object use already enforces object safety. Integrated source/effect-contract/effect-compiler tests passed 121 tests, alongside the worker's focused, downstream, policy and supported-target checks. No timing or extra SIMD claim is made.

Test value: the strengthened cents survivor catches a declared default losing its intrinsic flag while preserving both endpoints; the strengthened ratio survivor catches an omitted exact round maximum alongside its already-independent default check. The rewritten control-record budget test rejects either exceeding the declared 64-byte ceiling or changing the twelve-word prepared-target payload contract; it no longer pins incidental Rust layout. Each preserves the useful assertion from a deleted duplicate without introducing a scenario that merely mirrors implementation. No owner question remains for this crate.
